draft.title: Justice in civil disputes
card: The process is fair. Each side knows the case against it, can put its own side and has the case decided without bias.
Everyone is treated equally in the process, with the same chance to be heard. Equality does not mean every party gets the same outcome.
People can understand their rights and use the system. Cost, distance, delay and complex rules can block access.
A civil dispute can fail on one of these three without failing on the others. For example, a fair hearing is of no use to a person who cannot afford to bring the case.
draft.remember: A just civil dispute needs a fair process, equal treatment and access to the system.

a.q: Which situation is mainly a problem of access in a civil dispute?
opts: A tenant cannot afford the fees to start a claim
A judge shows bias toward one side at a hearing
One party is not told the case against it
One party is given less time to speak than the other
a.why: Being unable to afford to start a claim stops the person from using the system at all. The other three are problems with how the hearing itself is run, so they concern fairness or equality. Cost is the barrier to access.
a.clue: Which person is kept out before any hearing begins?

b.q: Priya has a strong claim against a builder. The court process is fair, but the rules are so complex she cannot work out how to file it. Which idea is most clearly lacking?
opts: Access, as she cannot use the system
Fairness, as the court is biased against her
Equality, as the builder gets a better result
Fairness, as she was not told of the claim
b.why: The process itself is fair, but Priya cannot use it because the rules are too complex. That is a failure of access. The tempting option is fairness, but nothing in the case shows bias or a denied chance to be heard.
b.clue: The process is fine. What stops Priya reaching it?

a.best: A tenant cannot afford the fees to start a claim

b.best: Access, as she cannot use the system
